title: Japanese joinery
why: Temples built with interlocking joints and no nails, some standing for over a thousand years.

title: Wooden gears and marble machines
why: Matthias Wandel builds machines out of plywood, including a wooden combination lock.

title: Kumiko
why: Lattice panels made from hundreds of tiny pieces held together by fit alone.

title: Green woodworking
why: Carving spoons and bowls from freshly cut wood with an axe and a knife, no workshop needed.

title: Reading tree rings
why: Dendrochronology dates old buildings, paintings and past climates from the pattern of rings in timber.

title: Yakisugi
why: A Japanese way of preserving cladding by charring its surface. Also called shou sugi ban.

title: The Windsor chair
why: A chair built from green and dry wood so that it tightens itself as it seasons.

title: Steam bending
why: Wood left in steam goes soft enough to bend into curves and keeps the shape when it cools.

title: Marquetry
why: Pictures made from thin slices of different woods, with the grain doing the shading.

title: Lutherie
why: Building violins and guitars, where a fraction of a millimetre of wood changes the sound.

title: Timber framing
why: Barns and halls held together by pegged joints, raised by a whole village in a day.

title: Coppicing
why: Cut certain trees to the ground and they grow back as straight poles, for centuries.

title: Bog oak
why: Timber preserved in peat for thousands of years, dug up black and nearly as hard as stone.

title: Shaker furniture
why: Furniture made by a religious community that treated plainness and usefulness as a duty.

title: Japanese puzzle boxes
why: Boxes that open only after a secret sequence of sliding moves, sometimes dozens of them.

title: Stave churches
why: Wooden churches in Norway that have stood since the Middle Ages, dragon heads and all.

title: The pole lathe
why: A lathe powered by a springy branch and your foot. Chair makers used them out in the woods.

title: John Harrison's wooden clocks
why: Before he solved the longitude problem, this carpenter built clocks almost entirely from wood.

title: Cooperage
why: Making watertight barrels from staves, with no glue and no nails.

title: Clinker boats
why: Hulls made from overlapping planks. It is how the Vikings built their longships.
